subject: Customer confirmation: review of misrouted telemetry and data integrity
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@barnabyholdings.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@barnabyholdings.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Possible log routing anomaly seen in our SIEM - asking for confirmation

Sergio,

Our security team flagged a routing anomaly in our SIEM this morning that referenced telemetry buckets with a Redwood prefix. Can you confirm whether any customer records (PII or transaction logs) could have been accessible externally or copied to a third party? We need an initial statement for our procurement/audit folks while you investigate.

We saw an IP address (198.51.100.23) performing a short GET on one object around 00:54 UTC — we don't know if that was a legitimate platform health check or something else.

Appreciate a quick confirmation that no customer data was exposed, or next steps if otherwise.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of InfoSec, Barnaby Holdings
elena.morales@barnabyholdings.com

---
This is a high-priority request from our side; they asked us to acknowledge within 24 hours.
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@barnabyholdings.com>, security@barnabyholdings.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:36:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Possible log routing anomaly seen in our SIEM - asking for confirmation

Thanks Elena — looping in Security and Infra to triage immediately. Initial notes:
- On quick check our telemetry router showed a transient misroute of diagnostic telemetry to an internal staging bucket (t-telemetry-staging) between 00:51–00:55 UTC.
- The staging bucket is private, not externally browsable, and access controls remained intact. No public ACL was ever applied.
- No signed URLs were issued for objects in that window.

Mina / Irene / Marcus: please run the full log sweep (S3 access logs, load-balancer logs, router audit trail) for 00:45–01:15 UTC, produce checksums of objects present at the time, and confirm whether any external principal authenticated (and if so, by which key/role). Attach initial evidence summary. We need a short customer-ready paragraph confirming whether customer records were affected.

Elena, I'll come back with a customer-ready affirmation as soon as we complete the sweep. For transparency we'll attach a high-level summary (no raw logs) and a signed integrity statement.

- Sergio
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@barnabyholdings.com>, security@barnabyholdings.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Possible log routing anomaly seen in our SIEM - asking for confirmation

Sergio — results from the log sweep (summary):

1) Scope and timeline- Window inspected: 2027-01-14 00:45:00 UTC through 2027-01-14 01:15:00 UTC- Affected object set: 23 diagnostic objects in t-telemetry-staging; none were customer production payloads (these are router heartbeats and aggregated metrics).

2) Access controls and access events- S3 server access logs: 1 GET request from 198.51.100.23 at 00:54:07 UTC targeting diagnostics/heartbeat-20270114-0053.json. The request used a valid internal service account (svc-router-collector) key and completed with 200.- No external-authenticated principals observed. The request originated from an internal NAT egress IP range mapped to our fleet health-checkers.

3) Integrity checks- We computed SHA256 checksums for the 23 objects and compared them to the manifest snapshot captured at 00:50:00 UTC (hash_manifest.txt attached). All checksums match — no modifications detected.

4) Artifact evidence attached- initial-log-scan-summary.csv — consolidated timeline and event counts- s3_access_log_excerpt.txt — access log lines for the window (redacted internal IPs)- hash_manifest.txt — file name → SHA256 mapping and signature of the manifest by our sysadmin PGP key

5) Chain-of-custody and mitigation- We logged all worker hostnames and keys that accessed the staging bucket in the incident ticket (INC-2027-0123). All keys involved are short-lived ephemeral service tokens issued by our control plane.- Root cause: router misrouting rule triggered during a staging deployment push; change has been reverted and we've added a pre-deploy gates check to prevent rule drift.

Conclusion (short, customer-facing): Based on the log sweep and checksum verification, Barnaby Holdings customer records were not present in the staging bucket and there is no evidence of unauthorized access or data exfiltration. We will provide a signed integrity affirmation for your audit.

If you'd like, we can provide the manifest and a signed statement for your security team to archive (we will not provide raw diagnostic payloads).

— Mina Haddad
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: initial-log-scan-summary.csv; s3_access_log_excerpt.txt; hash_manifest.txt
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@barnabyholdings.com>, security@barnabyholdings.com
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: FINAL: Formal integrity affirmation for incident on 2027-01-14 — Barnaby Holdings

Elena / Barnaby security team,

Thank you for flagging this. Please find our formal affirmation below and the signed artifact attached (integrity-affirmation-statement.pdf).

Formal affirmation (executive summary):
Redwood Inference has completed a forensic sweep of infrastructure telemetry and storage logs related to the misrouting of diagnostic telemetry to an internal staging bucket on 2027-01-14 between 00:51–00:55 UTC. The investigation included S3 access logs, load-balancer connection traces, router audit trails, and SHA256 checksum verification of objects present in the staging bucket.

Findings:
- Objects present in the staging bucket were diagnostic telemetry and aggregated heartbeats; no customer production records were present.
- Access to the staging objects during the incident window was performed by internal service principals; no external authentication or anonymous access was detected.
- Checksum comparison against a manifest snapshot taken at 00:50:00 UTC shows no modifications to objects discovered in the bucket.

Conclusion: Based on the evidence collected, there is no indication of customer data exposure, exfiltration, or unauthorized access. Redwood is providing a signed integrity affirmation and a redacted evidence bundle for your audit.

Remediation and prevention:
- The misrouting rule has been reverted and a pre-deploy gating check added to the router config pipeline.- Additional monitoring alerts for staging bucket access patterns deployed.

If your audit or procurement team requires any additional signed materials or a phone call to walk through the evidence, we are available.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0184

Attachments: integrity-affirmation-statement.pdf (signed), initial-log-scan-summary.csv (redacted), hash_manifest.txt
